source.text: ה֚וֹי אֲרִיאֵ֣ל אֲרִיאֵ֔ל קִרְיַ֖ת חָנָ֣ה דָוִ֑ד סְפ֥וּ שָׁנָ֛ה עַל־שָׁנָ֖ה חַגִּ֥ים יִנְקֹֽפוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Woe, Ariel, Ariel, town [where] camped David! Add year to year; festivals let them go around.

en.L: Woe, Ariel, Ariel, [the] town [where] David camped! \q Add year to year; let [the] festivals go around.
en.B: Woe to Ariel, Ariel, the town where David made camp! \q Add one year to another; let the festivals come around again.
en.R: How terrible it will be for Ariel, for Ariel, the city of Jerusalem where David camped! \q Go on adding one year to the next. Keep holding your festivals as they come around.

decisions.choice: Ariel: a name for Jerusalem, most likely meaning "altar hearth"
decisions.reason: The same word names the hearth of the altar in Ezekiel 43:15-16, and verse 2 plays on that sense. The city is the one where David camped (verse 1) and is Mount Zion (verse 8). The word can also mean "lion of God" (2 Samuel 23:20). The name is kept so the wordplay in verse 2 can be seen.

decisions.choice: where David camped: Jerusalem, which David captured and made his city
decisions.reason: David took the stronghold of Zion and lived there (2 Samuel 5:6-9). The verb "camp" returns in verse 3, where God himself camps against the city.

decisions.choice: add year to year; let the festivals go around: let the yearly round of feasts go on as usual
decisions.reason: The words may be ironic: the city keeps its festivals while judgment comes, perhaps within a year (32:10). Worship that is only routine is condemned in verse 13 (1:13-14).

decisions.choice: the city of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable names the city that verse 8 calls Mount Zion, so the reader knows who Ariel is.

source.text: וַהֲצִיק֖וֹתִי לַֽאֲרִיאֵ֑ל וְהָיְתָ֤ה תַֽאֲנִיָּה֙ וַֽאֲנִיָּ֔ה וְהָ֥יְתָה לִּ֖י כַּאֲרִיאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will bring distress to Ariel, and there will be mourning and moaning, and she will be to me like an altar hearth.

en.L: And I will bring distress on Ariel, \q and there will be mourning and moaning, \q and she will be to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} like [an] altar hearth.
en.B: Then I will press Ariel hard; \q there will be mourning and moaning, \q and she will be to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} like an altar hearth.
en.R: But I will bring trouble on Ariel. \q Her people will weep and cry. \q To {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, the city will be like an altar where the fire burns.

decisions.choice: like an altar hearth: a wordplay on the name Ariel
decisions.reason: The city called Ariel will become a real "ariel", an altar hearth where fire burns and victims die. Its suffering is pictured as a sacrifice laid on God's altar (34:6).

decisions.choice: mourning and moaning: loud grief
decisions.reason: The two nouns come from the same root and sound alike, as they do in Lamentations 2:5.

decisions.choice: like an altar where the fire burns
decisions.reason: Readable explains "altar hearth" as the place on the altar where the fire burns.

source.text: וְחָנִ֥יתִי כַדּ֖וּר עָלָ֑יִךְ וְצַרְתִּ֤י עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ מֻצָּ֔ב וַהֲקִֽימֹתִ֥י עָלַ֖יִךְ מְצֻרֹֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will encamp like the circle against you, and I will besiege against you [with] a post, and I will raise against you siege-works.

en.L: And I will camp like a ring against you, \q and I will lay siege against you [with] posts, \q and I will raise siege works against you.
en.B: I will camp in a ring all around you; \q I will hem you in with siege posts \q and set up siege works against you.
en.R: I will set up my camp all around you. \q I will close you in with guard posts. \q I will build ramps and towers to attack your walls.

decisions.choice: I will camp: God himself becomes the besieger
decisions.reason: David once camped at this city (verse 1); now God camps against it. The army that surrounds it is in his service (10:5-6).

decisions.choice: like a ring: on every side
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means a circle or ball (22:18). The Septuagint reads "like David", from almost the same letters, linking back to verse 1.

decisions.choice: posts ... siege works: the structures of an army besieging a city
decisions.reason: The first word means something set up, such as a post or palisade; the second, works raised against walls, such as ramps or towers (2 Kings 25:1).

decisions.choice: build ramps and towers to attack your walls
decisions.reason: Readable names the kinds of siege works an army raised against a city.

source.text: וְשָׁפַלְתְּ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ תְּדַבֵּ֔רִי וּמֵֽעָפָ֖ר תִּשַּׁ֣ח אִמְרָתֵ֑ךְ וְֽ֠הָיָה כְּא֤וֹב מֵאֶ֨רֶץ֙ קוֹלֵ֔ךְ וּמֵעָפָ֖ר אִמְרָתֵ֥ךְ תְּצַפְצֵֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will be low; from [the] ground you will speak, and from [the] dust your speech will be low, and your voice will be like a spirit of the dead from [the] ground, and from [the] dust your speech will whisper.

en.L: And you will be brought low; from [the] ground you will speak, \q and from [the] dust your words will come low, \q and your voice will be like [that of a] spirit of the dead from [the] ground, \q and from [the] dust your words will chirp.
en.B: Brought low, you will speak from the ground; \q your words will come muffled from the dust. \q Your voice will rise from the earth like a ghost's, \q and from the dust your words will chirp.
en.R: You will be knocked to the ground. You will speak from down in the dust, and your words will be hard to hear. \q Your voice will sound like a ghost speaking from under the ground. \q Your words will be a faint whisper from the dust.

decisions.choice: a spirit of the dead: the voice that mediums claimed to call up from the ground
decisions.reason: The same word is used at 8:19, where such spirits "chirp and mutter" (1 Samuel 28:7-14). The proud city will be so weak that its voice sounds like a faint ghostly whisper from the earth.

decisions.choice: chirp: speak in a thin, faint voice
decisions.reason: The verb is used of birds (10:14; 38:14) and of spirits of the dead (8:19).

decisions.choice: Brought low, you will speak from the ground
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the first two clauses so the poem's pairs of lines stand out.

source.text: וְהָיָ֛ה כְּאָבָ֥ק דַּ֖ק הֲמ֣וֹן זָרָ֑יִךְ וּכְמֹ֤ץ עֹבֵר֙ הֲמ֣וֹן עָֽרִיצִ֔ים וְהָיָ֖ה לְפֶ֥תַע פִּתְאֹֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be like dust fine the multitude of your strangers, and like chaff passing away the multitude of ruthless ones; and it will be in an instant, suddenly.

en.L: But the multitude of your foreigners will be like fine dust, \q and like passing chaff the multitude of [the] ruthless; \q and it will happen in an instant, suddenly.
en.B: Yet the horde of your foes will be like fine dust, \q the horde of the ruthless like chaff that blows away. \q It will happen in a moment, all at once.
en.R: But all the enemies who attack you will be blown away like fine dust. \q The crowds of cruel soldiers will be like chaff that the wind carries off. \q It will happen in a moment, very suddenly.

decisions.choice: your foreigners: the foreign enemies who attack the city
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "your strangers", the foreign armies of verse 7. The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) reads "your arrogant ones", from a similar-looking word.

decisions.choice: a sudden turn: the attackers themselves are scattered
decisions.reason: After verses 1-4 describe the siege, verse 5 turns: the horde that surrounds the city is blown away like dust and chaff (17:13). The last clause leads into God's coming in verse 6.

decisions.choice: all the enemies who attack you / the crowds of cruel soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable explains "your strangers" and "the ruthless" as the enemy armies.

source.text: מֵעִ֨ם יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ תִּפָּקֵ֔ד בְּרַ֥עַם וּבְרַ֖עַשׁ וְק֣וֹל גָּד֑וֹל סוּפָה֙ וּסְעָרָ֔ה וְלַ֖הַב אֵ֥שׁ אוֹכֵלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: From with [the] LORD of hosts it will be visited with thunder and with earthquake and a sound great, storm-wind and tempest and a flame of fire devouring.

en.L: From {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts she will be visited \q with thunder and with earthquake and [a] great noise, \q [with] whirlwind and tempest and [the] flame of devouring fire.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies will come to her \q with thunder, earthquake, and a mighty roar, \q with gale and tempest and the blaze of a fire that consumes.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies will come to the city. \q He will come with thunder, earthquakes, and a loud roar. \q He will come with strong winds and storms and a fire that burns everything up.

decisions.choice: she will be visited: the LORD will come to the city in power
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to come to someone in help or in punishment. The storm and fire here strike the enemy, who vanish like a dream (verses 5, 7), so the visit rescues the city, though it is also a fearful judgment. Some read the line as judgment on the city itself.

decisions.choice: thunder, earthquake, storm and fire: the signs that God himself is coming
decisions.reason: God's coming is described with storm, quake and fire at Sinai (Exodus 19:16-18) and in Psalm 18:8-16 and 30:27-30.

decisions.choice: will come to her
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who acts, since the passive "she will be visited from the LORD" is hard to follow.

decisions.choice: will come to the city
decisions.reason: Readable names the city and repeats "He will come" to break the long list into short sentences.

source.text: וְהָיָ֗ה כַּֽחֲלוֹם֙ חֲז֣וֹן לַ֔יְלָה הֲמוֹן֙ כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם הַצֹּבְאִ֖ים עַל־אֲרִיאֵ֑ל וְכָל־צֹבֶ֨יהָ֙ וּמְצֹ֣דָתָ֔הּ וְהַמְּצִיקִ֖ים לָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be like a dream, a vision of the night, the multitude of all the nations going to war against Ariel, and all going to war against her and her stronghold and those distressing her.

en.L: And it will be like a dream, a vision of [the] night, \q the multitude of all the nations that wage war against Ariel, \q and all who wage war against her and her stronghold, and who distress her.
en.B: Then the horde of all the nations that make war on Ariel, \q all who attack her and her stronghold and press her hard, \q will be like a dream, like something seen in the night.
en.R: Armies from all the nations will fight against Ariel. \q They will attack the city and its fortress and bring it trouble. \q But they will disappear like a dream, like something you see at night while you sleep.

decisions.choice: like a dream, a vision of the night: gone as quickly as a dream
alternatives: the siege will seem only a bad dream
decisions.reason: A dream disappears when the sleeper wakes (Job 20:8; Psalm 73:20). The vast enemy army will vanish just as completely.

decisions.choice: her and her stronghold: the city and its fortress
decisions.reason: The pronouns are feminine and refer to Ariel, the city. The third verb is the same one God uses of himself in verse 2: the nations distress the city as God's instruments.

decisions.choice: the attack first, then the vanishing
decisions.reason: Readable tells who attacks before saying that they vanish, so the comparison is clear.

source.text: וְהָיָ֡ה כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ יַחֲלֹ֨ם הָרָעֵ֜ב וְהִנֵּ֣ה אוֹכֵ֗ל וְהֵקִיץ֮ וְרֵיקָ֣ה נַפְשׁוֹ֒ וְכַאֲשֶׁ֨ר יַחֲלֹ֤ם הַצָּמֵא֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה שֹׁתֶ֔ה וְהֵקִיץ֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה עָיֵ֔ף וְנַפְשׁ֖וֹ שׁוֹקֵקָ֑ה כֵּ֣ן יִֽהְיֶ֗ה הֲמוֹן֙ כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם הַצֹּבְאִ֖ים עַל־הַ֥ר צִיּֽוֹן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it will be just as dreams the hungry, and there! eating, and he awakes and empty his appetite; and just as dreams the thirsty, and there! drinking, and he awakes and there! faint and his throat longing; so will be the multitude of all the nations going to war against the mountain of Zion.

en.L: And it will be just as [when] the hungry dreams, and look, [he is] eating, and he wakes, and his appetite [is] empty; \q and just as [when] the thirsty dreams, and look, [he is] drinking, \q and he wakes, and look, [he is] faint, and his throat [is] craving; \q so will be the multitude of all the nations that wage war against Mount Zion.
en.B: It will be like someone hungry who dreams of eating, then wakes and the stomach is still empty; \q like someone thirsty who dreams of drinking, then wakes weak, the throat dry and craving. \q That is how it will be for the horde of all the nations that make war on Mount Zion.
en.R: A hungry person may dream about eating, but then wake up still hungry. \q A thirsty person may dream about drinking, but then wake up weak and still thirsty. \q It will be like that for the armies of all the nations that fight against Mount Zion. They will not get what they hoped for.

decisions.choice: the dreamer: the attacking nations, who wake to find they have nothing
decisions.reason: Verse 7 compared the attackers to a dream; here they are the dreamers. They think the city is theirs to devour, but they wake empty-handed. Jerusalem's rescue from Sennacherib's army in 701 BC is told in 37:36-37.

decisions.choice: appetite, throat: the word for the living self, used of hunger and thirst
decisions.reason: The word often means "soul" or "life" but can mean throat or appetite (5:14). Here it is the empty stomach and the dry throat.

decisions.choice: They will not get what they hoped for.
decisions.reason: Readable states the point of the comparison, which the first meaning decision explains.

source.text: הִתְמַהְמְה֣וּ וּתְמָ֔הוּ הִשְׁתַּֽעַשְׁע֖וּ וָשֹׁ֑עוּ שָֽׁכְר֣וּ וְלֹא־יַ֔יִן נָע֖וּ וְלֹ֥א שֵׁכָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Delay and be astounded! Blind yourselves and be blind! They have become drunk and not wine; they have staggered and not strong drink.

en.L: Stall, and be stunned; blind yourselves, and be blind! \q [They] are drunk, but not [with] wine; \q [they] stagger, but not [with] strong drink.
en.B: Go slow and stand stunned; make yourselves blind and stay blind! \q They are drunk, though not with wine; \q they reel, though not from strong drink.
en.R: Go ahead, be slow and confused! Close your eyes and stay blind! \q The people are drunk, but not from wine. They stumble around, but not from any strong drink.

decisions.choice: commands spoken in irony: since you refuse to see, stay blind
decisions.reason: The prophet orders what the people are already doing. This is the hardening announced at 6:9-10, and verse 10 says the LORD has brought it about.

decisions.choice: stall: linger, hesitate in a daze
decisions.reason: The verb means to delay or hesitate (Genesis 19:16). Paired with "be stunned", it pictures people too dazed to act.

decisions.choice: drunk, but not with wine: their stupor comes from God, not drink
decisions.reason: In 28:7 the priests and prophets reel from real wine. Here the drunkenness is the spirit of sleep of verse 10 (51:21).

decisions.choice: The people
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are, since the verse moves from "you" to "they".

source.text: כִּֽי־נָסַ֨ךְ עֲלֵיכֶ֤ם יְהוָה֙ ר֣וּחַ תַּרְדֵּמָ֔ה וַיְעַצֵּ֖ם אֶת־עֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם אֶת־הַנְּבִיאִ֛ים וְאֶת־רָאשֵׁיכֶ֥ם הַחֹזִ֖ים כִּסָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For has poured out on you [the] LORD a spirit of deep sleep, and he has shut your eyes, the prophets, and your heads, the seers, he has covered.

en.L: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has shut your eyes, the prophets; \q and your heads, the seers, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has covered.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has poured over you a spirit of heavy sleep. \q He has shut your eyes, that is, your prophets; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has wrapped your heads, that is, your seers.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has made you fall into a deep sleep. \q The prophets are like your eyes, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has shut them. \q The seers are like your heads, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has covered them.

decisions.choice: a spirit of deep sleep: a heavy sleep sent by God
decisions.reason: The same word is used of the sleep God sent on Adam (Genesis 2:21) and on Abram (Genesis 15:12). Paul cites this verse with Deuteronomy 29:3 in Romans 11:8.

decisions.choice: your eyes, the prophets; your heads, the seers: the prophets are the nation's eyes
decisions.reason: The prophets and seers should see for the people. God has closed and covered them, so no one sees. The phrases stand beside "eyes" and "heads" to explain them.

decisions.choice: The prophets are like your eyes ... The seers are like your heads
decisions.reason: Readable states the comparison so the picture is clear.

source.text: וַתְּהִ֨י לָכֶ֜ם חָז֣וּת הַכֹּ֗ל כְּדִבְרֵי֮ הַסֵּ֣פֶר הֶֽחָתוּם֒ אֲשֶֽׁר־יִתְּנ֣וּ אֹת֗וֹ אֶל־יוֹדֵ֥עַ סֵ֛פֶר לֵאמֹ֖ר קְרָ֣א נָא־זֶ֑ה וְאָמַר֙ לֹ֣א אוּכַ֔ל כִּ֥י חָת֖וּם הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And has become to you the vision of all like the words of the scroll the sealed, which they give it to [one who] knows writing, saying, Read please this, and he says, Not I am able, for sealed [is] it.

en.L: And the vision of all [this] has become for you like the words of the sealed scroll, which [people] give to [one who] knows writing, saying, "Read this, please," and he says, "I cannot, for it [is] sealed."
en.B: This whole vision has become for you like the words of a sealed scroll. People hand it to someone who can read and say, "Please read this," and the answer comes, "I cannot; it is sealed."
en.R: This whole message from God has become like a scroll that is sealed shut. Suppose you give it to someone who knows how to read and say, "Please read this." That person will say, "I cannot. It is sealed."

decisions.choice: the sealed scroll: a rolled document closed with a seal
decisions.reason: A scroll was rolled up and sealed with clay or wax so that only the right person could open it (Jeremiah 32:10-14). Isaiah's own teaching was bound and sealed among his disciples (8:16). The people cannot take in the message God gives them.

decisions.choice: knows writing: knows how to read
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has "the writing"; the reading tradition has "writing", meaning one who can read, as in verse 12.

decisions.choice: This whole message from God
decisions.reason: Readable explains "vision" as the message God gave the prophet (1:1).

decisions.choice: the answer comes / that person will say
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable avoid "he", since the reader may be anyone.

source.text: וְנִתַּ֣ן הַסֵּ֗פֶר עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־יָדַ֥ע סֵ֛פֶר לֵאמֹ֖ר קְרָ֣א נָא־זֶ֑ה וְאָמַ֕ר לֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְתִּי סֵֽפֶר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And is given the scroll to [one] who not knows writing, saying, Read please this, and he says, Not I know writing.

en.L: And the scroll is given to [one] who does not know writing, saying, "Read this, please," and he says, "I do not know writing."
en.B: Or the scroll is handed to someone who cannot read, with the words, "Please read this," and the answer comes, "I do not know how to read."
en.R: Or suppose you give the scroll to someone who does not know how to read and say, "Please read this." That person will say, "I cannot read."

decisions.choice: the learned and the unlearned alike: no one in the nation receives the message
decisions.reason: The reader will not break the seal and the unlearned cannot read. Either way the vision stays closed, because of the blindness of verses 9-10. Verse 18 promises a day when the deaf will hear the words of a scroll.

decisions.choice: the answer comes / that person will say
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, Balanced and Readable avoid "he" for a person who may be anyone.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲדֹנָ֗י יַ֚עַן כִּ֤י נִגַּשׁ֙ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה בְּפִ֤יו וּבִשְׂפָתָיו֙ כִּבְּד֔וּנִי וְלִבּ֖וֹ רִחַ֣ק מִמֶּ֑נִּי וַתְּהִ֤י יִרְאָתָם֙ אֹתִ֔י מִצְוַ֥ת אֲנָשִׁ֖ים מְלֻמָּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] Lord, Because that has drawn near the people this with its mouth, and with its lips they have honored me, and its heart it has made far from me, and has been their fear of me a commandment of men taught,

en.L: And [the] Lord said: Because this people draws near with its mouth, \q and with its lips they honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q but its heart it keeps far from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and their fear of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is a command of humans [that has been] taught,
en.B: The Lord said: Since this people approaches {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with words of the mouth \q and gives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} honor with their lips \q while keeping their heart far from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and the fear they show {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is only a human rule learned by rote,
en.R: The Lord said: These people come close to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with their words. \q They praise {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with their lips, but their hearts are far away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q When they worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, they are only following rules that people have taught them.

decisions.choice: honor with the lips, a heart far away: Jesus applies this verse to the religious leaders of his day
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes it in Matthew 15:8-9 and Mark 7:6-7 against keeping human tradition while setting aside God's command. Those Gospels follow the Septuagint, whose last line reads that they worship God in vain, teaching human commands and teachings.

decisions.choice: their fear of me: their worship and reverence for God
decisions.reason: "Fear of the LORD" is the whole of a person's reverence and service (11:2; Proverbs 1:7). Here it has become rules repeated without the heart.

decisions.choice: because ... therefore: the reason here leads into the judgment of verse 14
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 14, which begins "therefore".

decisions.choice: When they worship me
decisions.reason: Readable says "worship" for "fear", the sense the second meaning decision gives.

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן הִנְנִ֥י יוֹסִ֛ף לְהַפְלִ֥יא אֶת־הָֽעָם־הַזֶּ֖ה הַפְלֵ֣א וָפֶ֑לֶא וְאָֽבְדָה֙ חָכְמַ֣ת חֲכָמָ֔יו וּבִינַ֥ת נְבֹנָ֖יו תִּסְתַּתָּֽר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: therefore here I [am], he will again do wonderfully with the people this, wonderfully and wonder; and will perish the wisdom of its wise, and the understanding of its understanding ones will hide itself.

en.L: therefore, look, I will again do wonders with this people, wondrously and [with] wonder; \q and the wisdom of its wise [ones] will perish, \q and the understanding of its discerning [ones] will hide itself.
en.B: therefore I will once again deal with this people in astonishing ways, marvel after marvel. \q The wisdom of their wise will come to nothing, \q and the insight of their discerning will disappear from sight.
en.R: So I will again do amazing things to these people, one surprising thing after another. \q The wisdom of their wise people will be lost. \q The understanding of their clever people will disappear.

decisions.choice: wonders: astonishing acts of God, here acts of judgment
decisions.reason: The word is used of God's great deeds (25:1; Exodus 15:11) and of the child's name in 9:5. Here the wonder is a judgment that leaves the nation's wise men helpless (28:29).

decisions.choice: the wisdom of the wise will perish: God brings human wisdom to nothing
decisions.reason: Paul quotes this line in 1 Corinthians 1:19, following the Septuagint, which reads "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise". Judah's wise counselors planned to trust Egypt (verse 15; 30:1-2).

decisions.choice: here I am, he will again: God speaks of himself with an unusual verb form
decisions.reason: After "here I" the verb is third person. The sense is plain: God will act again.

source.text: ה֛וֹי הַמַּעֲמִיקִ֥ים מֵֽיהוָ֖ה לַסְתִּ֣ר עֵצָ֑ה וְהָיָ֤ה בְמַחְשָׁךְ֙ מַֽעֲשֵׂיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מִ֥י רֹאֵ֖נוּ וּמִ֥י יוֹדְעֵֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Woe, those who make deep from [the] LORD to hide counsel, and is in a dark place their deeds, and they have said, Who sees us? and who knows us?

en.L: Woe, those who go deep to hide [their] counsel from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and their deeds are in a dark place, \q and they say, "Who sees us? And who knows us?"
en.B: Woe to those who burrow deep to keep their schemes hidden from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q Their deeds are done in a dark place, \q and they say, "Who sees us? Who knows about us?"
en.R: How terrible it will be for people who try hard to hide their plans from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q They do their work in the dark. \q They say, "No one sees us. No one knows what we are doing."

decisions.choice: counsel: a secret plan, likely the plan to seek help from Egypt
decisions.reason: The leaders of Judah made plans without asking the LORD, sending envoys to Egypt (30:1-2; 31:1).

decisions.choice: Who sees us? Who knows us?: they think God does not notice
decisions.reason: The same boast is made by the wicked in Psalm 94:7 and Ezekiel 8:12. Verse 16 answers it: the maker knows what he has made.

decisions.choice: No one sees us. No one knows what we are doing.
decisions.reason: Readable turns the questions into the statements they imply.

source.text: הַ֨פְכְּכֶ֔ם אִם־כְּחֹ֥מֶר הַיֹּצֵ֖ר יֵֽחָשֵׁ֑ב כִּֽי־יֹאמַ֨ר מַעֲשֶׂ֤ה לְעֹשֵׂ֨הוּ֙ לֹ֣א עָשָׂ֔נִי וְיֵ֛צֶר אָמַ֥ר לְיוֹצְר֖וֹ לֹ֥א הֵבִֽין׃

records.literal_gloss: Your perversity! If like the clay the potter will be regarded, that will say a thing made to its maker, Not he made me, and a thing formed said to its former, Not he has understood?

en.L: Your perversity! Is the potter to be regarded as the clay, \q that [the] thing made should say of its maker, "He did not make me," \q and [the] thing formed say of its potter, "He has no understanding"?
en.B: How you turn everything on its head! \q Is the potter to be counted the same as the clay? \q Should the thing that was made say of its maker, "He did not make me"? \q Should the vessel say of the one who shaped it, "He has no sense"?
en.R: You have everything backward! \q God made you as a potter makes a pot. But you treat {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} were no better than the clay. \q A pot cannot say about the one who made it, "He did not make me." \q It cannot say about the potter, "He does not know what he is doing."

decisions.choice: your perversity: you turn things upside down
decisions.reason: The word means overturning. Treating the maker as if he were the clay reverses the order of creation.

decisions.choice: the potter and the clay: God is the maker and his people are what he made
decisions.reason: The picture returns in 45:9 and 64:7 and in Jeremiah 18:1-6. Paul uses it in Romans 9:20-21. Those who hide their plans (verse 15) act as if God did not make them and could not understand them.

decisions.choice: say of its maker: the speaker talks about the maker, not to him
decisions.reason: The words quoted are in the third person ("He did not make me"), so the preposition here means "about".

decisions.choice: God made you as a potter makes a pot.
decisions.reason: Readable states who the potter and the clay stand for, as the second meaning decision explains.

source.text: הֲלוֹא־עוֹד֙ מְעַ֣ט מִזְעָ֔ר וְשָׁ֥ב לְבָנ֖וֹן לַכַּרְמֶ֑ל וְהַכַּרְמֶ֖ל לַיַּ֥עַר יֵחָשֵֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: Not yet a little little, and will turn Lebanon into the orchard, and the orchard to the forest will be regarded?

en.L: [Is it] not yet a very little while, \q and Lebanon will turn into [an] orchard, \q and the orchard will be regarded as [a] forest?
en.B: Is it not only a little while longer before Lebanon becomes orchard land, \q and the orchard land is counted a forest?
en.R: In a very short time, the wild forest of Lebanon will become rich orchard land. \q And the orchard land will grow as thick as a forest.

decisions.choice: Lebanon into orchard, orchard into forest: a great reversal in the land
decisions.reason: The wild forest becomes cultivated land, and cultivated land grows as thick as a forest. The picture is of a coming change in which the low are lifted (verses 18-21); 32:15 uses the same words for a land renewed by the Spirit.

decisions.choice: orchard: a planted, fruitful field or garden land
decisions.reason: The word also names Mount Carmel, known for its fertile slopes (33:9; 35:2). The same word is "orchard" at 10:18.

decisions.choice: In a very short time ...
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it expects.

source.text: וְשָׁמְע֧וּ בַיּוֹם־הַה֛וּא הַחֵרְשִׁ֖ים דִּבְרֵי־סֵ֑פֶר וּמֵאֹ֣פֶל וּמֵחֹ֔שֶׁךְ עֵינֵ֥י עִוְרִ֖ים תִּרְאֶֽינָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will hear in the day that the deaf [the] words of a scroll, and from gloom and from darkness [the] eyes of [the] blind will see.

en.L: And in that day the deaf will hear [the] words of [a] scroll, \q and out of gloom and out of darkness [the] eyes of [the] blind will see.
en.B: On that day the deaf will hear the words written in a scroll, \q and blind eyes will see, out of the gloom and the dark.
en.R: At that time, people who are deaf will hear the words written in a scroll. \q People who are blind will come out of the darkness and see.

decisions.choice: the deaf will hear the words of a scroll: the closed message of verses 11-12 is opened
decisions.reason: The scroll no one could read (verses 11-12) will be heard. The blindness God sent (verses 9-10; 6:10) will be undone (35:5; 42:7). Jesus points to the deaf hearing and the blind seeing as signs of his work (Matthew 11:5).

decisions.choice: the deaf, the blind: people who could not take in God's word
decisions.reason: The words describe the spiritual deafness and blindness of verses 9-12, and also bodily healing, as 35:5-6 shows.

source.text: וְיָסְפ֧וּ עֲנָוִ֛ים בַּֽיהוָ֖ה שִׂמְחָ֑ה וְאֶבְיוֹנֵ֣י אָדָ֔ם בִּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יָגִֽילוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will add humble ones in [the] LORD joy, and [the] needy of mankind in [the] Holy One of Israel will rejoice.

en.L: And [the] humble will add joy in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and [the] needy of humankind will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.
en.B: The humble will have more and more joy in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and the neediest of humankind will be glad in the Holy One of Israel.
en.R: Humble people will be filled with more joy because of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q The poorest people will be happy because of the Holy One of Israel.

decisions.choice: will add joy: their joy will grow
decisions.reason: The verb "add" means to increase or to do again. The poor, who were wronged (verses 20-21), will find joy in the LORD.

decisions.choice: the humble, the needy: the poor and the oppressed
decisions.reason: The words describe people without power, who are cheated in court (verse 21; 11:4; 32:7).

source.text: כִּֽי־אָפֵ֥ס עָרִ֖יץ וְכָ֣לָה לֵ֑ץ וְנִכְרְת֖וּ כָּל־שֹׁ֥קְדֵי אָֽוֶן׃

records.literal_gloss: For will come to an end [the] ruthless, and will be finished [the] mocker, and will be cut off all those watching for wickedness,

en.L: For [the] ruthless will come to an end, and [the] scoffer will be finished, \q and all who watch for wickedness will be cut off,
en.B: For the ruthless will be gone and the scoffer finished, \q and all who are on the watch for a chance to do wrong will be cut off,
en.R: This will happen because the cruel will be gone. People who sneer at others will disappear. \q All who look for chances to do evil will be destroyed.

decisions.choice: the scoffer: one who mocks God's word and those who keep it
decisions.reason: The scoffers of 28:14 and 28:22 rule Jerusalem and mock the prophet's message.

decisions.choice: those who watch for wickedness: those eager for a chance to do harm
decisions.reason: The verb means to stay awake and watchful, as God "watches" over his word in Jeremiah 1:12. These people stay alert for evil.

decisions.choice: This will happen because
decisions.reason: Readable spells out how "for" links this verse to the joy of the poor in verse 19.

source.text: מַחֲטִיאֵ֤י אָדָם֙ בְּדָבָ֔ר וְלַמּוֹכִ֥יחַ בַּשַּׁ֖עַר יְקֹשׁ֑וּן וַיַּטּ֥וּ בַתֹּ֖הוּ צַדִּֽיק׃ס

records.literal_gloss: those making sin a man with a word, and for the one reproving in the gate they lay a snare, and they turn aside with emptiness [the] righteous.

en.L: those who make a person a sinner by a word, \q and for the one who reproves in the gate they lay a snare, \q and they turn aside [the] righteous with emptiness.
en.B: those who make a person guilty with a single word, \q who set snares for the one who speaks up for justice in the gate, \q and with baseless claims turn the innocent away.
en.R: They make others look guilty by lying about them. \q They try to trap anyone who speaks up for what is right in court. \q They use false arguments so that innocent people do not get justice.

decisions.choice: the one who reproves in the gate: the person who stands up for justice in the town court
decisions.reason: Elders heard cases at the town gate (Ruth 4:1-2). Amos 5:10 uses the same words: people hate the one who reproves in the gate.

decisions.choice: emptiness: baseless claims, false arguments
decisions.reason: The word means emptiness or chaos (Genesis 1:2; 41:29). Here it is a case without substance, used to deny the innocent their right (10:2).

decisions.choice: those who make a person a sinner: these describe the wicked of verse 20
decisions.reason: The verse continues the list begun in verse 20.

decisions.choice: by lying about them
decisions.reason: Readable explains "with a word" as false testimony, the sense that "emptiness" at the end of the verse confirms.

decisions.choice: in court
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the gate was where cases were heard.

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּדָ֖ה אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֑ם לֹֽא־עַתָּ֤ה יֵבוֹשׁ֙ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְלֹ֥א עַתָּ֖ה פָּנָ֥יו יֶחֱוָֽרוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says [the] LORD to the house of Jacob who redeemed Abraham: Not now will be ashamed Jacob, and not now his face will grow pale.

en.L: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to the house of Jacob, who redeemed Abraham: \q Jacob will not now be ashamed, \q and his face will not now grow pale.
en.B: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who redeemed Abraham, says this about the house of Jacob: \q From now on Jacob will not be disgraced; \q his face will not turn pale anymore.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who rescued Abraham, has a message for the people of Jacob. This is what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says: \q Jacob's people will not be ashamed anymore. \q Their faces will not turn pale with fear anymore.

decisions.choice: who redeemed Abraham: the LORD who freed Abraham
decisions.reason: This is the only place Scripture speaks of Abraham being redeemed. It may recall God bringing him out of Ur and the gods his family served (Genesis 12:1; Joshua 24:2-3).

decisions.choice: to the house of Jacob: to or about the descendants of Jacob
decisions.reason: The preposition can mean "to" or "concerning"; the words that follow speak about Jacob in the third person.

decisions.choice: his face will not grow pale: Jacob will not turn white with fear or shame
decisions.reason: Jacob stands for the people descended from him, pictured as an ancestor who no longer has to watch his family disgraced (verse 23).

decisions.choice: Jacob's people
decisions.reason: Readable says "Jacob's people" for Jacob as the nation.

decisions.choice: the LORD, who redeemed Abraham
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable place the description next to the LORD, whom it describes.

source.text: כִּ֣י בִ֠רְאֹתוֹ יְלָדָ֞יו מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדַ֛י בְּקִרְבּ֖וֹ יַקְדִּ֣ישֽׁוּ שְׁמִ֑י וְהִקְדִּ֨ישׁוּ֙ אֶת־קְד֣וֹשׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְאֶת־אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יַעֲרִֽיצוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For when he sees his children, the work of my hands, in his midst, they will sanctify my name, and they will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and the God of Israel they will regard with awe.

en.L: For when he sees his children, the work of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hands, in his midst, they will hold {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name holy, \q and they will hold the Holy One of Jacob holy, \q and the God of Israel they will regard with awe.
en.B: For when Jacob sees his children around him, children {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hands have made, they will keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name holy. \q They will honor the Holy One of Jacob as holy \q and tremble with awe before the God of Israel.
en.R: Jacob's people will see their children around them, the children I have made. Then they will honor {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name as holy. \q They will honor the Holy One of Jacob as holy. \q They will be filled with awe before the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: his children, the work of my hands: the descendants God gives Jacob
decisions.reason: Jacob, the ancestor, sees a new family that God himself has made (19:25; 60:21). Some read "the work of my hands" as the deeds God has done among them.

decisions.choice: sanctify my name: treat God as holy, in worship and obedience
decisions.reason: This answers the empty honor of verse 13 and echoes 8:13, where the LORD of hosts is the one to regard as holy and to fear.

decisions.choice: Jacob
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jacob, the one who sees, since the pronoun alone is unclear.

source.text: וְיָדְע֥וּ תֹֽעֵי־ר֖וּחַ בִּינָ֑ה וְרוֹגְנִ֖ים יִלְמְדוּ־לֶֽקַח׃

records.literal_gloss: And will know those going astray of spirit understanding, and those murmuring will learn insight.

en.L: And those who go astray in spirit will know understanding, \q and those who grumble will learn teaching.
en.B: People whose spirits have strayed will gain insight, \q and the grumblers will take teaching to heart.
en.R: People who were confused will understand. \q People who complained will be willing to learn.

decisions.choice: those who grumble: people who complain against God
decisions.reason: The same verb describes Israel grumbling in their tents in the wilderness (Deuteronomy 1:27; Psalm 106:25).

decisions.choice: those who go astray in spirit: those whose minds have wandered from the truth
decisions.reason: Here "spirit" is the mind and will. The blindness of verses 9-12 is undone, and the people learn what they once refused (28:9).

decisions.choice: People who were confused
decisions.reason: Readable explains "go astray in spirit" as confusion of mind.
